body:
WHAT
When a user-role message contains an image block, the OpenAI-compatible provider serializes it as the multimodal `content` array: a text part plus one `image_url` part per image with a `data:<mediaType>;base64,<data>` URL, in the same user message as its text. A message with no image is still sent as a plain string `content`.

WHY
Every image used to be flattened to '[image omitted]', so a vision-enabled workspace sent nothing and got confident commentary on an unseen picture; servers that never learned the array form must keep receiving strings.

WHERE
engine/providers/src/openai-compat.ts — toWireMessages(system, messages): the `images.length > 0` branch building { role: "user", content: [{ type: "text" }, { type: "image_url", image_url: { url: `data:${b.mediaType};base64,${b.data}` } }] }, the `else if (text)` string branch; type WireContentPart; flattenToolResult() (tool-role results still flatten images to '[image omitted]' — tool results are described upstream by Session.describeToolImages).

TEST CHECKLIST
1. toWireMessages('', [{ role: 'user', content: [{ type: 'text', text: 'hi' }, { type: 'image', mediaType: 'image/png', data: 'AAAA' }] }]) yields one user message whose content is an array [{ type: 'text', text: 'hi' }, { type: 'image_url', image_url: { url: 'data:image/png;base64,AAAA' } }].
2. A user message with only text yields content as the plain string 'hi', not an array.
3. An image-only user message (no text) yields a content array with just the image_url part and no empty text part.
4. Two images in one message produce two image_url parts in order, in the same user message (not two messages).
5. A tool_result whose content has an image part is flattened to text containing '[image omitted]' by flattenToolResult (documenting that the tool path relies on Session.describeToolImages upstream).
